evidence.location: Decision point 1, participant turn re: alternatives
evidence.quote: I could've rung the foreman again on the trackside phone to get him to re-walk it, or got the on-call technician out to test the circuit, or gone to pilotman working as a precaution.
evidence.explanation: The worker generates and compares distinct courses of action under time and operational constraints, weighing costs (delay to 6M42, arranging pilotman working) against risk, which is planning and non-routine resolution rather than a single prescribed step.

evidence.location: Decision point 3, participant turn re: 2T19 routing
evidence.quote: Send it through on the affected signal relying on backup indication and the driver's caution, divert it onto the loop line which adds six minutes, or hold it at the previous station until the fault's diagnosed.
evidence.explanation: The worker constructs and evaluates multiple contingent action sequences with different timing and resource trade-offs for an unfamiliar fault, characteristic of planning/resolution rather than routine choice.

evidence.location: Decision point 4, participant turn re: pilotman working
evidence.quote: Suspend normal working and go to pilotman working for everything through that section until it's properly looked at.
evidence.explanation: The worker adapts the overall control method for the section in response to a non-routine, undiagnosed problem, reorganising the sequence of future train movements.

secondary_categories.subcategory: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation

evidence.quote: That circuit's had three nuisance trips in the last eight months, all rain or leaf-fall related, all logged.
evidence.explanation: The worker retrieves and evaluates historical maintenance-log information to interpret a current indication.

evidence.quote: I finally got hold of the on-call technician, who told me the circuit's wiring has a known moisture-sensitivity problem that's never been fully run down.
evidence.explanation: The worker actively seeks out and obtains diagnostic information from another source to resolve an open question.

secondary_categories.subcategory: A2.1 Uncodified visual or auditory information processing

evidence.location: Decision point 1, description of track circuit signal
evidence.quote: Shortly after the handback, the track circuit for the section showed occupied for about four seconds, then cleared. It did that twice in ten minutes.
evidence.explanation: The worker interprets an intermittent, non-fully-codified perceptual signal (a fluctuating indication) rather than applying an explicit deterministic rule.

evidence.quote: the transmission was garbled by static. I caught "clear" and something like "trolley," but it wasn't a full clean readback.
evidence.explanation: The worker interprets degraded auditory information (a static-obscured radio transmission) and must judge its adequacy.

evidence.quote: that's the same signature — short blip, self-clears, no correlation with anything physically on the track.
evidence.explanation: The worker builds a mental model/category ("nuisance trip signature") from prior cases and applies it to classify a new instance, which is a diagnostic generalisation beyond simple information retrieval.

evidence.quote: get 6M42 through Falcon Bank and get 2T19 back on time without anyone sitting in a queue longer than they needed to
evidence.explanation: The worker allocates priority and sequencing between two competing train movements and coordinates with foreman, technician, and drivers, aligning multiple dependent actors toward safe, timely operation.

ambiguities: A3.4 (managing/coordinating) versus B2 (teamwork): the controller directs and sequences movements involving the foreman, technician, and drivers, which could be read as coordination of others' work (A3.4) or as reciprocal collaborative interaction (B2 teamwork). Both are recorded, with A3.4 as content and B2 as a method dimension, to avoid double-counting the same evidence under conflicting labels.

evidence.explanation: The controller has discretion to choose among several distinct courses of action (re-walk, technician test, pilotman working, or proceed) with no indication of requiring prior approval.

evidence.quote: No rule had actually been broken; the section was already possession-free by the book.

evidence.quote: the section was already possession-free by the book.

task_anchors.task_description: Interpreting an intermittent track-circuit occupancy signal against historical maintenance data and deciding whether to authorize freight movement or seek verification.
Evaluating the adequacy of a partially garbled radio readback against the already-completed formal handback.
Choosing among routing options for a passenger service facing an unfamiliar junction-signal fault.
Revising the control method for the section (to pilotman working) upon receiving new diagnostic information about the circuit fault.

evidence: Once I had it slotted into that nuisance-trip bucket in my head, verifying it didn't feel like it was really adding anything.
The handback itself was already formally done and clean at 23:40 — this was just the follow-up readback.
I didn't have any history on that particular fault to lean on, so I wasn't willing to trust backup indication on an unfamiliar problem.
I went to pilotman working... I wanted a person physically controlling movement rather than relying on the circuit again.
